Package io.mavlink4j.testkit

Class FakeVehicle

java.lang.Object
io.mavlink4j.testkit.FakeVehicle
All Implemented Interfaces:
AutoCloseable
public final class FakeVehicle extends Object implements AutoCloseable
A scripted aircraft over real UDP loopback: it dials the system under test, sends a heartbeat every 200 ms by default (one heartbeat can be lost on plain UDP while the far side is still binding, so the stream never stops), records every frame it receives, and answers on demand or by script.

Scripting

  • onCommand(MavCmd, CommandReply) — what to do when that command arrives; an unscripted command is recorded and left unanswered.
  • parameter(String, float, MavParamType) — makes a parameter exist; the vehicle then answers PARAM_REQUEST_READ, PARAM_REQUEST_LIST and PARAM_SET for it. An unknown name gets no reply, as on a real autopilot.
  • FakeVehicle.Builder.signedWith(byte[]) — the vehicle signs what it sends and verifies what it receives with that 32-byte key.
The reply* methods send one reply by hand, for cases a script cannot express (a wrong parameter name, an out-of-order ack).

Thread-safety: every public method may be called from the test thread while the vehicle's own heartbeat and reader threads run.

    • relocate

      public void relocate() throws IOException, InterruptedException
      Simulates this vehicle's transport address changing (a NAT rebind, a relay taking over): closes the current link and opens a fresh one to the same gateway under the identical MAVLink identity. Proves a caller re-resolves a peer's address on every send rather than caching it.
      Throws:
      IOException - if the new socket cannot be opened
      InterruptedException - if interrupted while the old reader stops
